content.value_statement: Survival analysis is hard when data includes censoring, competing events, and time-dependent evaluation. This skill guides practical scikit-survival workflows from preprocessing to model comparison.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable survival models, including Cox, Coxnet, ensemble models, and Survival SVMs.
Explains survival outcome creation, missing value handling, feature encoding, and scaling workflows.
Guides evaluation with concordance index, time-dependent AUC, and integrated Brier score.
Covers competing risks, cumulative incidence functions, and non-parametric survival estimators.
Shows how to combine scikit-survival with scikit-learn pipelines and cross-validation.
limitations: It does not install, execute, or verify scikit-survival in the user environment.
It does not replace statistical review, clinical validation, or regulatory approval.
It focuses on Python scikit-survival rather than R survival packages.
Model quality still depends on event counts, censoring patterns, and data quality.

use_cases.title: Plan a survival modeling workflow
use_cases.description: Choose preprocessing, model families, and evaluation metrics for censored time-to-event data.

use_cases.title: Evaluate clinical outcome models
use_cases.description: Compare Cox, ensemble, and SVM approaches with metrics that account for censoring.

use_cases.title: Build reproducible ML pipelines
use_cases.description: Use scikit-learn pipelines, cross-validation, and parameter tuning for survival prediction.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a first model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have right-censored survival data with event and time columns. Recommend a first scikit-survival model and explain the choice.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare survival data
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a preprocessing workflow for scikit-survival with categorical features, missing values, and feature scaling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare model performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a model comparison plan for Cox, Random Survival Forest, Gradient Boosting, and Survival SVM using censoring-aware metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design competing risks analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: I have multiple mutually exclusive event types. Help me structure a competing risks analysis and choose suitable outputs.

output_examples.input: A user asks which model to try for interpretable survival prediction with moderate censoring.
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation to start with a Cox model, check assumptions, and compare against an ensemble baseline.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to evaluate a survival model under high censoring.
output_examples.output: A metric plan using Uno concordance, time-dependent AUC, integrated Brier score, and censoring-aware cross-validation.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to handle competing events in a clinical dataset.
output_examples.output: A workflow that separates event types, estimates cumulative incidence, and avoids treating competing events as ordinary censoring.

best_practices: Validate event indicators, survival times, censoring rates, and event counts before modeling.
Use censoring-aware metrics and report more than one performance measure.
Compare interpretable and flexible models before selecting a final workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not treat competing events as simple censoring without checking the study question.
Do not use standard classification metrics for time-to-event prediction.
Do not tune hyperparameters on the test set or ignore censoring during validation.

faq.question: What is scikit-survival used for?
faq.answer: It is used for survival analysis and time-to-event modeling in Python with censored outcomes.

faq.question: Does this skill run my analysis automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and workflow structure for tools you run in your own environment.

faq.question: Can it help choose between Cox and ensemble models?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use interpretable Cox models and when to compare flexible ensemble methods.

faq.question: Does it cover model evaluation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers concordance index variants, time-dependent AUC, Brier score, and cross-validation patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with competing risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cumulative incidence and when competing risks methods are more appropriate.

faq.question: Is it limited to Claude?
faq.answer: No. The skill content is also relevant for Codex and Claude Code workflows.
